confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors rest on web searches. Those searches turned up crowdsourced Numbeo figures (via Expatica, June 2026): inexpensive meal about $20, three-course dinner for two about $95, cappuccino about $5.67, 0.5 L domestic draft beer about $7.25. Westword/Expatistan (Nov 2022) listed a downtown cocktail at about $13. I did not find a direct current price for cocktails or wine by the glass. I set cocktail at roughly 1.8x the restaurant beer price and a glass of wine at roughly 1.5x, which fits typical US urban relationships. Beer is nudged up from the Numbeo average because restaurant pints cost more than the crowdsourced figure. The FX rate is the RBA observation for 18 Nov 2026, the latest the search returned. I read it from search results, not by opening the RBA page. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Denver's market, including summer peak demand. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any listings, so those four anchors carry the most uncertainty. Hostel supply in Denver is limited, and hotel prices vary a lot by neighborhood and by event.
comparable_city_reasoning: Denver is a mid-to-high-cost large US city, about 9% above the US average per crowdsourced indexes. Its pricing is similar to Portland, Seattle and Minneapolis, a little below Boston or San Francisco.
